description: A finance director must authorize the settlement of an acquisition earn-out and finalize the payment, escrow, release timetable, and tax-remittance plan, with input from legal and tax.

shared_context.S1: The company completed the acquisition of Northstar Analytics last year.
shared_context.S2: The seller has submitted a $4,800,000 earn-out claim under the acquisition agreement.
shared_context.S3: The current draft settlement recommends paying the full claim at closing with no escrow and does not specify a tax-remittance timetable.
shared_context.S4: Mara must sign the binding settlement before the closing team releases funds.
shared_context.S5: Under the standard closing checklist, Mara asks legal and tax to review the settlement immediately before signing.

PF1.text: While reviewing the indemnity schedule this week, Jonas confirmed that an unresolved environmental claim entitles the company to retain exactly $1,200,000 of the earn-out in escrow for 90 days after closing; he recorded this in a working note that has not yet been circulated.

PF2.text: Leila received a tax memo this morning confirming that the earn-out is compensation subject to exactly 30% withholding and that the withheld amount must be remitted within exactly 10 business days; the memo has not yet been added to the closing checklist.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly $3,600,000 of the earn-out must be paid at closing.
Exactly $1,200,000 of the earn-out must be held in escrow.
The escrow must be released after exactly 90 days.
Exactly 30% withholding must be applied to the earn-out.
The withheld tax must be remitted within exactly 10 business days.
The settlement must include an earn-out escrow commitment and a tax-remittance commitment.
The legal escrow requirement and tax treatment must be cited in the decision justification.

decisive_facts.why: The draft pays the full $4,800,000 with no escrow; PF1 changes the payment to exactly $3,600,000, requires exactly $1,200,000 in escrow for exactly 90 days, and adds the escrow commitment.
The draft specifies no tax mechanics; PF2 changes withholding to exactly 30%, sets remittance to exactly 10 business days, and adds the tax-remittance commitment.
